label: August 1918
headline: The Black Day
deck: British, Dominion and French armies break the line before Amiens
caption: Tanks lead Canadian and Australian infantry out of the morning mist east of Amiens
body: At dawn on 8 August, without a preliminary bombardment, Canadian and Australian divisions with British and French armies on their flanks attack in fog east of Amiens. Some four hundred tanks go forward with them, and by evening the line has moved seven miles. Whole German battalions lay down their arms; General Ludendorff calls it the black day of the German army.

The blows do not stop. The British strike at Albert on 21 August and at Arras on the 26th; New Zealanders enter Bapaume on the 29th, and the Australians storm Mont St Quentin above Péronne on the last day of the month.
At Spa the German leaders agree that the war can no longer be won in the field, and that peace must be sought at a favourable moment.
briefs: Allied troops land at Archangel and at Vladivostok
Lenin is shot and wounded by Fanny Kaplan in Moscow
Zeppelin L70 is shot down off Norfolk with Peter Strasser aboard
